candidate.title: sci-MET
candidate.scope: The middle sci-MET row of the supplied Illumina schematic, resolved to the single-cell combinatorial indexing for methylation analysis architecture described by Mulqueen et al., Nature Biotechnology 36, 428–431 (2018), PMID 29644997, DOI 10.1038/nbt.4112. The scAba-Seq and scRC-Seq rows above and below are separate neighboring assays, not alternatives identified for the sci-MET card. Three drawn wells at each sorting stage are illustrative branches, not a specified experimental well count. Nuclei isolation/depletion and the combined bisulfite/linear-amplification/PCR block remain at the granularity drawn; the unlabelled depletion chemistry is not assigned to LAND or xSDS. The endpoint is a genomic-DNA-derived methylation library; the poster label Sequencing-ready cDNA is retained as an observation and resolved using the primary paper. Sequencing and computational analysis are readout interpretation, not added graph operations.

states.label: Pooled sequencing-ready genomic-DNA-derived library (poster label: Sequencing-ready cDNA)
features: Physical product: amplified DNA derived from bisulfite-treated genomic fragments, with sequencing adapters and combinatorial indexes.
Biological target: single-cell genomic cytosine methylation, including CG and CH contexts assessed in the primary study.

Interpretation: genomic insert sequence locates the assayed DNA, cytosine-conversion patterns support methylation assessment at covered bases, and combined transposase/PCR indexes assign fragments to intended cells.
The primary implementation reads one transposase index and two PCR indexes, combined into the cell barcode; the figure abstracts these as first and second well-specific indexing stages.

Per-cell coverage is sparse; barcode collisions can merge nuclei that share a first index and a second-round well. The library does not establish complete genome coverage or perfectly unique cell assignments.

operations.description: Process the material of second-round well a separately under the shared PCR-based tagging caption. Bisulfite treatment converts unmethylated genomic cytosines; linear amplification installs the second adapter, and PCR amplifies the resulting DNA while adding the second-stage well indexes and sequencing adapter sequences. operations.mechanism: Retain the broad block drawn. The paper resolves its consequential internal interfaces: bisulfite treatment precedes random primer extension; the extension primer carries part of the Illumina read 2 primer sequence; indexed PCR primers then add the second indexing stage. Two PCR-primer indexes implement that stage in the primary method. No additional physical sorting stage is implied.
operations.information_effect: Conversion status of genomic cytosines is carried into amplified DNA sequence for methylation readout. The surviving first-stage adapter/index and newly introduced PCR indexes preserve the connection between each sequenced genomic insert and its intended nucleus. Nuclei no longer serve as the compartmental carrier in the amplified library; second-round wells remain separate until the following pool.
